d021_target_investment_arithmetic.assumption: Four independent runs, each resetting treasury 55 and group cash 50/55. These runs must not be appended to, or combined with, D020 no-investment renewal tables. Every project is fully financed at start; builder payments are equal progress installments during construction; new ability begins the following month. Profits/taxes settle at month end and cannot fund that month starts. Group cash includes an untouched group-wide operating buffer 10, not one new buffer payment per plant. All comparisons remain pending; no gameplay acceptance.
d021_target_investment_arithmetic.b1_limitation: Deadline financing only: all second factories operate by M17/M23 as applicable. Some least-government-cost paths wait with zero subsidy. This does not establish D004 three-month output/profit/guardrail success or B1 matched routes being two months faster: the cheaper 29 route 1 path can operate as early as route 2. Enterprise preference and capital competition need future authorized rule replay.
d021_target_investment_arithmetic.excluded_costs_and_constraints: Public packages are minimum illustrative costs, not a proven complete playable route. Additional power, water, medical/service expansion, full road/port/transport chain, maintenance, land/water quotas, migration speed, skill/training capacity, order acquisition, material quantities, administrative slots and enterprise response are not priced or simulated. The D017 three-month reference material project is an independent generic throughput example, not these heterogeneous public projects or a construction schedule guarantee. Existing recurring envelope is held fixed; no new free public services are claimed.

29_route_1.assumption: Investment plans are locked to this target site by assumption, not an enterprise choice. Both factories are at this same candidate. Route 1 substitutes up to 200 existing imports; route 2 assumes cooperation and 100 export orders per factory are already available at operation, without implementing the cooperation rule. Each new factory has 100 previously idle domestic workers, working utilities, adequate housing/services, skills, land/water slots and demand on operation. Capital timing alone is checked; these physical and demand assumptions are unverified. No operational subsidy. Existing ordinary energy contracts continue; all new factories buy additional maritime energy privately. Both renewal offers are refused; aid stops at M13. No W water exemption, E long-contract purchase, enterprise AI, migration, pressure or todo implementation.

29_route_2.assumption: Investment plans are locked to this target site by assumption, not an enterprise choice. Both factories are at this same candidate. Route 1 substitutes up to 200 existing imports; route 2 assumes cooperation and 100 export orders per factory are already available at operation, without implementing the cooperation rule. Each new factory has 100 previously idle domestic workers, working utilities, adequate housing/services, skills, land/water slots and demand on operation. Capital timing alone is checked; these physical and demand assumptions are unverified. No operational subsidy. Existing ordinary energy contracts continue; all new factories buy additional maritime energy privately. Both renewal offers are refused; aid stops at M13. No W water exemption, E long-contract purchase, enterprise AI, migration, pressure or todo implementation.

factory_profit_arithmetic.assumption: Unimplemented arithmetic only. Orders equal actual production and sales, between 0 and nameplate output; no inventory, dynamic pricing or automatic order guarantee. Energy and gross-sales tax vary linearly with actual orders. Gross wages and other operating cost stay fixed for this monthly comparison; reduced staffing/closure is not simulated. Payroll tax is withheld from gross wages and is not another firm expense. No operating subsidy or corporate profit tax. Profit means operating surplus after proposed sales tax, excluding depreciation, capital amortization, financing and capital expenditure; it is not complete accounting net income. Energy passed through by government is charged only for energy the new factory actually uses; unused take-or-pay energy belongs to the government cost ledger.

renewal_fiscal_comparison.assumption: Matched 0/1/2 full-output factories in E and refusal. All reference workers come from previously idle domestic labor, so full factory payroll tax is incremental. Factories pay for their own energy; government only books E purchases and E sales, never deducts private energy costs twice. Refusal uses maritime energy privately, outside government budget. Excludes construction, subsidy and migration costs equally from both sides; this is a recurring-flow comparison, not a feasible investment timeline or B15. Renewed aid is assumed through M24 without any unconfirmed W fee; W effects on water/targets are not simulated.
